tested:
── Silver Peak / Aruba EdgeConnect (SilverEdge / VXOA) ────────────────────────
No profile existed for this vendor before 2026-07-18 - "silveredge"/"silver_peak"
matched no PROFILES key, so get_profile() fell back to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE
(512MB/1 vCPU). Live-reproduced: the real image (silveredge-8.1.9.6.tar,
VXOA 8.1.9.6) booted with a raw `qemu-system-x86_64 -m 512 -smp 1` never got
past the GRUB menu after 5.5+ minutes (0 bytes of further serial output,
QEMU process alive the whole time - not a crash, a boot that never progresses
under memory pressure). The identical image at -m 4096 -smp 2 reached a full
"silverpeak login:" VXOA prompt in under 4 minutes. Same "unknown vendor
silently gets the 512MB generic floor" failure class already fixed for isrv/
NX-OS/FortiGate above (see those comments) - min/default set from the PROVEN
4096MB/2-vCPU boot, not a vendor-doc guess.

reasons.nic:
NIC e1000 -> virtio-net-pci (NPX-824, 2026-09-05). Evidence, not a guess: EVE-NG
PRO v7's own production template for this exact image says `qemu_nic:
virtio-net-pci` (docs/reference/eveng-implementation/raw/templates/silveredge.yml), so a
shipping product has run this guest on virtio for years - the driver is in the
image. e1000 is emulated packet-by-packet in userspace and can never use the
kernel fast path; virtio can (vhost-net, NPX-823). Live-booted on netplex before
this landed - run recorded in docs/status/PLATFORM-AUDIT.md NPX-824.
